shape_verdict_rationale: I checked the substrate-shadow reading against the atlas's OWN holographic edges and it FAILS for this gap. E023 (AdS/CFT, CFT->GR, E2 duality) and E024 (Ryu-Takayanagi, CFT->entanglement-geometry, E2 currency-shadow-price) DO establish that in the atlas a higher-altitude object (bulk GEOMETRY) can be the shadow of a deeper substrate (boundary ENTANGLEMENT). But those edges are about GRAVITY/GEOMETRY being entanglement's shadow -- they say NOTHING about the SM gauge GROUP being a shadow of any substrate. No atlas edge casts SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1) as the shadow of a deeper layer. So importing the holographic 'geometry is a shadow' template here would be unlicensed analogy, not atlas-internal evidence. The licensed reading is the opposite altitude: the missing layer is a PARENT that the SM is a shadow OF (by specialization), and the gap is that the parent's SELECTION content is absent -- corroborated by E037 below.
role_profile: P2 Constraints -- DOMINANT: the missing layer's core job is constraint-selection. Anomaly-freedom is a P2 constraint that prunes the candidate space; the additional discrete selection rule is a further P2 constraint (or a P2 constraint induced by a P5 packaging) that collapses the surviving set to one point. The SM card itself places the gauge group in the 'inputs/constraints' slot, confirming P2 is where the missing distinction lives.

P5 Packaging -- the selection may be realized as a packaging/completion that has SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1) as its (discrete) fixed point: a U_f that reconstructs a unique (G,R) from a higher datum (a GUT-breaking pattern, a compactification topology). If selection is dynamical, P5 carries it.

P6 Audit -- a defect ledger over the candidate space (which (G,R) violate consistency, by how much) is needed to make 'pruning' monotone and checkable; anomaly coefficients are exactly such a nonnegative ledger.

P3 Protocol/holonomy -- ACTIVATED ONLY IF selection is route/path-dependent (e.g. landscape selection depends on cosmological history): then a non-decaying route-mismatch would type the obstruction as genuinely non-localizable. Flagged as conditional, not asserted.
P1 Operator-rewrite -- NOT centrally activated: the gap is not a forced effective term in a macro evolution; it is a discrete missing label.
P4 Staging -- NOT centrally activated: no continuous scale parameter generates the group (contrast E0, where P4/staging carries the run).

divergence.explanation: FIREWALL SPLIT FIRST: the audit marks divergence_is_casting_artifact=true. The honest reconciliation is that this casting-dependence bites ONLY on a substrate-shadow framing of E019 -- which the card explicitly fences off below (no atlas edge casts the gauge group as a shadow of a deeper substrate). The FIRM finding survives the firewall untouched: the conventional parent supplies STRUCTURE without the SELECTION PRINCIPLE, so the missing layer sits one rung ABOVE it -- and this rests on the SCORED E3 tier of E037 in the atlas, not on any contested holographic import or on the particular (G,R)-before-the-lens casting. Now the body: The conventional candidate -- a GUT (SU(5)/SO(10)) above the SM, or string compactification fixing the gauge group -- has the RIGHT ALTITUDE and the RIGHT DIRECTION (a richer parent ABOVE the SM from which the SM descends by specialization, exactly L's shape). To that extent the fresh structural read MATCHES convention: SBT independently says 'look for a selection-carrying parent above,' which is what a GUT/compactification is. But it DIVERGES on the decisive structural point: a GUT or a string vacuum supplies STRUCTURE (a larger group, a Calabi-Yau) without supplying the SELECTION PRINCIPLE, so it does not actually close the gap -- it relocates it one rung up (now: 'why THIS GUT?' / 'why THIS vacuum?'). SBT's required predicate #3 (a discrete selection rule beyond consistency) is precisely the thing GUTs/strings lack. So the honest verdict is: convention names the right KIND of layer but mistakes a structure-provider for a selection-provider. The missing layer is the SELECTION FUNCTIONAL itself, which sits ABOVE even the conventional candidate.

audit.verdict: CASTING-DEPENDENT (downgraded from the card's implied discovery-grade reading to 'contested/casting-conditional'), but DEFENSIBLE and notably honest -- NOT an overclaim. The card survives the firewall on the points that matter most: (1) NO content overclaim -- it rigorously stays at shape, refuses to name the missing theory, and even cites the retro-atlas disclaimer that SBT retrodicts nothing new here; (2) all cited evidence exists and the decisive corroborator (E037: the conventional GUT/string parent is ITSELF foreclosed E3 for the landscape/selection reason) is real and accurately read; (3) the out-of-sample joint-selection test is genuine and falsifiable with a discriminating historical control. The divergence-from-convention HOLDS but is DEFLATIONARY, not field-redirecting: the claim is that convention under-delivers (names a structure-provider, not a selection-provider), which the atlas's own E037 confirms -- this is the framework working as a firewall, not manufactured excitement. CRUCIALLY, the divergence is SUBSTANTIALLY a casting artifact, and the card itself flags this (READING B): the 'parent-above / which-group-is-an-input' shape is largely built into the conservative SM casting that fixes (G,R) before the lens, and the altitude verdict is largely forced by the pre-frozen emergence-up arrow rather than independently derived. So divergence_is_casting_artifact:true. The honest terminal label is 'partial-match, CASTING-CONDITIONAL', exactly as the discipline demands -- the card mostly earns this but should foreground the casting-dependence as a co-headline rather than a secondary reading, and must stop recruiting E016's procedural within-layer E3 as inter-layer evidence. With the six required-hardening fixes (de-double-count the frozen arrow, promote the casting caveat, fix the E016 over-read, disambiguate the up/down dual framing, mark the OOS test's partial internality, and disclose the anti-control status), this is a solid, scope-respecting missing-layer card. Score 3.5/5: not field-redirecting (and it correctly does not claim to be), but a clean, auditable, honestly-hedged characterization of the hole's shape that does not slip into reductionism.
